newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Labour Party pledges no more NZ asset sales.
newsitem.headline: Labour Party pledges no more NZ asset sales.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party pledged on Thursday not to sell any more state assets if it becomes government.

Finance spokesman Michael Cullen said the recent sales of Forestry Corp and Works Corp completed the asset sales programme begun by the fourth Labour government and he could see no good reason for any further privatisation of state assets.
"We didn't get into the selling business just for the sake of it," he said in a statement.

"We got into it because there were very real fiscal risks to the Crown from the continued involvement in industries like telecommunications, banking and forestry, and because we needed to reduce debt."
Cullen said the sale of Telecom by Labour had broken a key election promise, and the party had been duly punished for it.
But he said the sale also introduced competition and new technology to the sector, and created new jobs and new businesses.

He said Labour had concerns about the speed and tendering process involved in the sale of the forestry cutting rights, but the party would not be involved in any deal to buy them back, as other political parties were promising.
"I have now completed a review of the remaining state assets and it will be my intention to recommend to an incoming Labour-led government that there be no further state asset sales."
Assets which could be sold include Television New Zealand, New Zealand Post and the electricity generators ECNZ and Contact Energy.
Cullen said Labour would examine the state owned enterprise model for each entity to ensure the legislation allowed them to operate to meet Labour's economic, environmental and social objectives.
